'''Sujatha Ramdorai''' (born 1962)<ref>Birth year from [http://www.isni.org/isni/0000000116051441 ISNI authority control file], retrieved 2018-12-01.</ref> is an [[Algebraic number theory|algebraic number theorist]] known for her work on [[Iwasawa theory]].  She is a professor of mathematics and [[Canada Research Chair]] at [[University of British Columbia]], [[Canada]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=2643|title=Canada Research Chairs|last=Government of Canada|first=Industry Canada|date=2012-11-29|access-date=2017-06-20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.ubc.ca/~sujatha/|title=Mathematics|website=www.math.ubc.ca|access-date=2017-06-20}}</ref> She was previously a professor at [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]].

==Education==
She completed her B.Sc. in 1982 at St. Joseph's college, Bangalore and then got her M.Sc. through correspondence from [[Annamalai University]] in 1985. After that she went for PhD at [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] and was awarded her PhD under supervision of [[Raman Parimala]] in 1992.<ref>[http://www.math.tifr.res.in/~sujatha/cv.html Homepage CV]</ref> Her dissertation was "Witt Groups of Real Surfaces and Real Geometry".

==Career==
Dr. Ramdorai initially worked in the areas of algebraic theory of quadratic forms and arithmetic geometry of elliptic curves.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://nobelprizeseries.in/tbis/s-ramdorai|title=Sujatha Ramdorai {{!}} The Best of Indian Science|website=nobelprizeseries.in|access-date=2019-02-16|archive-date=15 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190215221240/http://nobelprizeseries.in/tbis/s-ramdorai|url-status=dead}}</ref> Together with [[John H. Coates|Coates]], Fukaya, [[Kazuya Kato|Kato]], and Venjakob she formulated a non-commutative version of the main conjecture of [[Iwasawa theory]], on which much of the foundation of this important subject is based.<ref>[http://www.abelprisen.no/en/nyheter/artikler/sujatha.html Interview with Sujatha]</ref> [[Iwasawa theory]] has its origins in the work of a great Japanese mathematician, [[Kenkichi Iwasawa]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gonitsora.com/an-interview-with-prof-sujatha-ramdorai/|title = An Interview with Prof. Sujatha Ramdorai|date = 28 December 2011}}</ref>

She holds an adjunct professorship position at [[Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Pune]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.iiserpune.ac.in/research/disciplines/mathematics|title=IISER Pune|website=www.iiserpune.ac.in|access-date=2017-06-20}}</ref>

Working with her husband Srinivasan Ramdorai and Indian mathematics writer V.S. Sastry, Sujatha Ramdorai conceived of and partially funded the [[Ramanujan Math Park]] in [[Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh]], which was inaugurated at the end of 2017.  The park is dedicated to mathematics education and honors the great Indian mathematician [[Srinivasa Ramanujan]] (1887-1920).

She is a member of the Scientific Committee of several international research agencies such as the Indo-French Centre for Promotion of Advanced Research, Banff International Research Station, International Centre for Pure and Applied Mathematics. She was a member of the [[National Knowledge Commission]] from 2007 to 2009. She is at present a member of the Prime Minister's Scientific Advisory Council from 2009 onwards and also a member of the National Innovation Council.<ref>[http://gonitsora.com/an-interview-with-prof-sujatha-ramdorai/ An Interview with Prof. Sujatha Ramdorai, http://GonitSora.com]</ref> She is also on the advisory board of [[Gonit Sora]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gonitsora.com/about-us/|title=About Us|date=10 April 2011 }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Ramdorai became the first Indian to win the prestigious [[ICTP]] [[ICTP Ramanujan Prize|Ramanujan Prize]] in 2006. She was also awarded the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award]], the highest honour in scientific fields by the Indian Government in 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/sujatha-ramdorai/|title=Sujatha Ramdorai – European Women in Mathematics|language=en-US|access-date=2019-02-16}}</ref> She is also the recipient of the 2020 [[Krieger–Nelson Prize]] for her exceptional contributions to mathematics research.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2020/Krieger-Nelson|title = Dr. Sujatha Ramdorai to receive the 2020 Krieger-Nelson Prize}}</ref> She has been bestowed with [[Padma Shri]] award by the Government of India for 2023 in the field of science and engineering.<ref>{{cite web |title=Padma Awards 2023 announced |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1893797 |website=Press Information Bureau |publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt of India |access-date=26 January 2023}}</ref>

==Editorial position==
*Managing editor, [[International Journal of Number Theory|''International Journal of Number Theory'' (''IJNT'')]] 
*Editor, ''Journal of Ramanujan Mathematical Society'' (''JRMS'')<ref>[http://www.math.tifr.res.in/~sujatha Homepage]</ref>
*Associate editor, ''Expositiones Mathematicae''<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.journals.elsevier.com/expositiones-mathematicae/editorial-board/sujatha-ramdorai/ |title=Sujatha Ramdorai, Associate Editor - Expositiones Mathematicae |website=www.journals.elsevier.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160320152433/http://www.journals.elsevier.com/expositiones-mathematicae/editorial-board/sujatha-ramdorai |archive-date=2016-03-20}}</ref>
